items.note: 'Bejouga' is taken to be the old form 'Bijuga/Bijouga' of the Bijagós, which fits the West African coastal route of the other notes. Moderate confidence: check the scan in case it is an OCR garble of something else.

items.place: About 53°N 9°E, Lower Elbe, Lower Saxony / Schleswig-Holstein, Germany
items.note: 53°N 9°E taken literally is inland, between Bremen and Hamburg. Whole degrees probably means 53°xx′N 9°xx′E, which takes in the Lower Elbe (Stade–Brunsbüttel). The birds are land birds, including Crested Lark, a species absent from Ireland, which rules out reading E as W (western Ireland). The examples show a voyage from here to n1458 between 7 a.m. and 2 p.m.

items.place: About 54°N 10°E, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany (Kiel Bay / Neumünster area)
items.note: Taken literally, 54°N 10°E is near Neumünster, inland. With truncated degrees it could be Kiel Bay (about 54°20′N). It ends the same 7 a.m.–2 p.m. passage as n1457. How the route went (Eider Canal or overland) is unknown.

items.place: At sea, tropical Atlantic (position garbled)
items.note: 'se? 43°.8. | 92350" W.' is badly garbled. One reading is 4°3′S 9°35′W, or it may be a misread of 1°43′S 9°30′W (n13). Sooty Terns place it in the tropical Atlantic. The exact position must be read from the page scan.

notes: None of the 22 items is a station of the scheme. They are all positions at sea or foreign places from the 1884 Ocean Notes. Things to check: (1) Kind for bare lat/long positions: I classed them as 'place' with the coordinates and an ocean description in place. If you would rather keep ship positions out of 'place', send them to a separate category. (2) n1473: the position is garbled, so read it from the scan. (3) n733: check whether '§.' is S or N. (4) n13: the '-' before the longitude is noise; confirm W. (5) n1457/n1458: whole-degree positions in north Germany that fall on land if taken literally. Crested Lark supports E rather than W, and the shared 7 a.m.–2 p.m. passage links them. Check the full text for the route (Elbe, Kiel). (6) n120 'Bejouga Islands' is taken as the Bijagós, Guinea-Bissau. Confirm from the scan. (7) n1073 'Schelling light-vessel' is taken as Terschelling, Netherlands. Confirm a light-vessel was there in 1884. (8) n1221/n1222 name the steamship Marathon and are classed 'none'. Each observation's position should come from its own lat/long or named place. (9) n207 covers the stretch from Cape Point to Algoa Bay, not one point.
